PATitle: Trainer guide: check receiving records against an ASN
PASubtitle: Logistics onboarding with a matched receipt and three exceptions
TargetAudience: New receiving clerks; delivered by a trainer.
ActivityDescription: Train clerks to compare a reported receipt with its advance ship notice before deciding whether its records match. The L&D assessment supplies the learning gaps and completion requirements; the engineering SOP supplies the records and decision rules. This guide turns those inputs into a demonstration, individual practice, and feedback.
TrainerGuidelines:
Explain the Notes boundaries before distributing records. Distinguish a logistics-unit ID from a product ID: one identifies the unit, the other its contents.
Demonstrate R1: locate unit 987654321000000012 in ASN-DEMO-01, compare KIT-A and 12 cases, then record Matched in exercise. Say explicitly that this is not receipt acceptance.
Ask learners what would change if the same product arrived on a different unit. Correct product-ID lookups and unsupported each-to-case conversions.
Observe each learner working through R1-R4. Use Validation for feedback and another attempt after a missed criterion; do not replace individual practice with a group answer.
DesiredLearningOutcome: Learners can compare the correct expected and reported records, distinguish a match from discrepancies or missing information, and produce a factual practice review card without accepting goods or altering records.
WhatIsNeeded:
Prepare ASN-DEMO-01, reported receipts R1-R4, blank comparison cards, the Receiving Review role card, and pencils or a local text editor.
Keep product, quantity, and unit of measure visible on both records. No conversion is supplied for R3; leave that gap visible.
Allocate the fictional 30-minute session supplied by the assessment. No scanner, account, physical goods, or stock-system connection is needed.
SkillsBasedLearningObjectives:
Distinguish a logistics-unit ID from a product ID and locate the exact ASN entry.
Compare product ID, quantity, and unit of measure without inventing expected values or conversions.
Record the correct exercise outcome and send exceptions or clarification questions to Receiving Review through the trainer.
DocumentationAndReferences:
L&D assessment A1-A3: audience and learning need, required skills, and observable completion requirements.
Engineering SOP SOP-DEMO-LOG-01, S1-S4: synthetic records, comparison rules, materials, and exercise boundaries. Both sources are in logistics-sources.json.
Public task and training-design research is documented in docs/CASE_STUDY.md. The local rules and records are fictional; source connections are manually curated, not AI-generated citations.
ActivitySteps:
Trainer briefing: explain why common receipt checks matter, identify the two kinds of ID, and set the simulation boundaries.
Trainer demonstration: complete the R1 comparison card while explaining each lookup and comparison; show why matching records is not goods acceptance.
Learner practice: each learner compares R1-R4 independently and records expected and reported values, outcome, and any Receiving Review question on a practice card.
Trainer feedback: compare cards with Validation. Discuss the difference between 8 and 7 cases, why 4 cases cannot be equated to 48 each without a conversion, and what to do when a unit is not on the ASN.
Retry and completion: learners correct missed criteria with another attempt and explain why an exception can be the right result. Record exercise completion only, not warehouse qualification.
Validation:
R1: unit 987654321000000012 maps to KIT-A, 12 cases expected and 12 cases reported. Outcome: Matched in exercise; no exception route is needed.
R2: unit 987654321000000029 maps to KIT-B, 8 cases expected and 7 cases reported. Outcome: Discrepancy; record both values and address the card to Receiving Review.
R3: unit 987654321000000036 maps to KIT-C, 4 cases expected and 48 each reported. Outcome: Needs clarification; ask Receiving Review for the approved each-to-case conversion. Do not assume equality or a numerical discrepancy across unlike units.
R4: unit 987654321000000043 has no matching entry in ASN-DEMO-01. Outcome: Needs clarification; preserve KIT-D and 2 cases as reported and ask Receiving Review whether the unit belongs on the ASN. Do not invent expected values.
Each card includes receipt ID, unit ID, ASN ID, expected and reported facts, outcome, and the required recipient or question. Each learner explains the unit/product distinction and meets every criterion; missed criteria require another attempt.
Expected and reported records remain unchanged. No real receipt approval, physical action, inventory update, or message occurs.
Notes:
Simulation only: compare fictional records. No goods handling, equipment use, barcode issuance, real receipt acceptance, inventory changes, or messages.
Stop if live systems, real shipment data, or physical handling are introduced; return to fictional materials.
This is prepared fixture replay, not a run of live AI, Copilot Studio, or Power Automate. Human review against BOTH sources is required before export. Completion does not qualify a learner for warehouse work.
The numeric identifiers are synthetic practice values, not issued GS1 keys. Rules, roles, allocation, and document metadata are authored fictional inputs, not measured research findings or operational authorization.
